MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  February 23, 2021
Due to COVID-19 and the “Stay at Home” Order for the State of California and the Social
Distance Guidelines issued by Federal, State, and Local Authorities this Council Meeting was
conducted via Video Teleconferencing for all Council and Staff with the exception of the City
Attorney and City Clerk who were present in the Council Chamber. All public comments that
were emailed to the City Clerk were read during the meeting.

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Kelley at
5:01 p.m., on February 23, 2021, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on February 18, 2021, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Teleconferenced:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Sachs
  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  None

Staff  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
Teleconferenced:  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services

Staff Present:  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

NEW BUSINESS

1.  Consideration of Advancing the Core Area (Downtown area) Improvement Plan: First
  Effort: Acquisition of Stein Mart Building for Creation of Public Paseo Entry to Oso
  Creek and Trail.

City Council Minutes  1  February 23, 2021
   City Attorney Bill Curley explained that the Brown Act requires that to consider acquisition
  of property, the Council must publicly make the decision that they wise to pursue negotiations.
  He outlined that several years ago the City undertook a downtown core area vision plan that
  foresaw the beneficial revitalization of the four corners at Marguerite and La Paz stretching
  down to Oso Parkway. The City Council is being asked if they have any interest in pursuing
  this negotiation. In Closed Session the Council will be asked for guidance on price and terms
  in starting negotiations with the property owner at this preliminary stage. Item 8 on this
  agenda would be after the Council makes the preliminary decision to pursue with negotiations
  on price and terms to authorize staff to start those negotiations.

  Barbara Hosmer, M.V.: Raised concerns regarding how this project will be funded and the
  smell and cleanliness of the riverbed.

  Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Pointed out that the residents are at a disadvantage that this item is not
  placed under regular business at 6:00 p.m. and that there is no staff report to view. She stated
  that the press release for the Core Area Vision Plan did not give notice to the public that this
  item was up for discussion this evening.

  Wendy Adams, M.V.: Stated that the residents of Mission Viejo should vote on this project
  before spending this sizable amount of money.

  Terrill Holland, M.V.: Pointed out that this should be voted on by the citizens of Mission
  Viejo. Expressed that this is an irresponsible use of public funds and is not in favor of the
  project.

  Robert Breton, M.V.: Stated that he supports this project and that it affords the City a unique
  opportunity to move forward with the Core Vision Plan. He pointed out the difficulty in
  dealing with 14 different owners who are more than content to collect their rents on old leases
  and who do not have incentive to invest in renovations to the village center.

  Motion made by Council Member Goodell, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum,
  Authorize the City to commence negotiation with Kinstler Family Trust to acquire the Stein
  Mart building for public park and open space use and to renovate the structure. Refer to staff
  report for Agenda item #8 for more information.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel - Anticipated Litigation: Initiation of Litigation
  Pursuant to Paragraph (4) of Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9 (1 cases)

CS2. Conference with Real Property Negotiators: Stein Mart Property 25282 Marguerite
  Parkway; Agency Negotiators: Dennis Wilberg, Keith Rattay, Elaine Lister, Cheryl

City Council Minutes  2  February 23, 2021
   Dyas and William Curley. Negotiating Party: Kinstler Family Trust. Under
  Negotiation-Price and Terms.

  Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Stated that the City is abusing its position of trust, power and authority
  regarding public support for the proposed $30 million Civic Core Vision Plan. She protests
  the Council and Executive Staff on their duties of a transparent government.

  Terrill Holland, M.V. Pointed out that this should be voted on by the citizens of Mission
  Viejo. Expressed that this is an irresponsible use of public funds and is not in favor of the
  project.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:13 p.m., Mayor Kelley recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:06 p.m. with five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that there was no reportable actions. The Council was given
updates on CS2 and CS1 was not addressed.

INVOCATION: Council Member Goodell

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Sachs

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Featured Business of the Month - Smart Cups LLC

  Presented proclamation to CEO & Founder Chris Kanik of Smart Cups LLC.

P2. Recognize 2020 Employee of the Year Krista Oberholtzer.

  Recognized Payroll and Accounting Technician Krista Oberholtzer.

P3. Mission Viejo Nadadores Update

  Received update.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Barbara Hosmer, M.V.: Asked the Council to look into a viable cable choice with Cox and perhaps
a senior discount. She also stated that the South Orange County cities should form a coalition for
power savings with SDGE.

City Council Minutes  3  February 23, 2021

NOES:  None

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

NEW BUSINESS (Continued)

8.  Exclusive 60-Day Negotiating Rights Agreement with the Kinstler Family Trust for the
  former Stein Mart Property, 25282 Marguerite Parkway, Village Center

  Director of Community Development Elaine Lister presented the staff report.

City Council Minutes  4  February 23, 2021
   Barbara Hosmer, M.V.: Raised concerns regarding how this project will be funded and the
  smell and cleanliness of the riverbed.

  Judy Bullockus, M.V.: Applauded the City for taking advantage to improve the Village
  Center. She stated she is in favor of Core Vision Plan.

  Helen Herr, M.V.: Stated that she agrees that the center needs an updating but does not agree
  with this project. She also asked when the citizens can put a vote to these types of projects.

  Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Pointed out that the staff report and the Oso Creek Shopping Center
  Revitalization Concept Video are very misleading. Asked why the press release did not
  inform the public that this item was on tonight’s agenda. Questioned if the City will be
  competing in the private market place and if the residents around the Civic Core area have
  been polled for their opinions about an amphitheater. She raised concerns of the relocation
  of the Santa Margarita Water District treatment plant and if those costs will be passed on to
  it’s ratepayers.

  Terrill Holland, M.V.: Pointed out that this should be voted on by the citizens of Mission
  Viejo. Expressed that this is an irresponsible use of public funds and is not in favor of the
  project.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to approve
  the Exclusive 60-Day Negotiating Rights Agreement with the Kinstler Family Trust (A21-
  07) for the former Stein Mart Property, Village Center, 25282 Marguerite Parkway.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  Received report from Mayor Kelley.

  Received report from Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum.

  Received report from Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum.

  Received report from Council Member Goodell.
City Council Minutes  5  February 23, 2021
 CITY MANAGER REPORT

13. COVID-19 Vaccine Distribution in Orange County

  City Manager Dennis Wilberg and Emergency Operations Manager Paul Catsimanes
  presented the staff report.

  By consensus the City Council received the report.

CITY ATTORNEY REPORT

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

14. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell shared that he has an upcoming OCTA Finance Administration
Committee tomorrow regarding sales tax revenues as it relates to transit options in the County and
it looks like sales tax revenues are down. He also stated that he has an Orange County Council of
Governments (OCCOG) Board of Directs meeting on Thursday and the Orange County Watershed
Management Agency Executive Committee meeting this week as well. Council Member Goodell
said he is working hard to stay informed representing the City in as many ways as he can.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths thanked City Staff for their volunteer work at Soka University assisting
with the vaccines. He thanked Keith Rattay on the slopes and mentioned Barbadanes Park looks
really good. Lastly, he thanked the Mayor on her first two months in office.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs stated that the City is in good shape and looks forward to working on the
budget in the upcoming months.

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum thanked City Staff for volunteering their time at the vaccine POD at Soka
University and food distribution that took place this past week. She said she is looking forward to
the Oso Fit Virtual 5K Fun Run and drive through Community Health Fair this Saturday at the
Norman P. Community center starting at 9:00 a.m. to Noon. Announced that the South Orange
County Economic Coalition is hosting a virtual event called “Give Me Shelter”, a forum on housing
in South Orange County on Friday February 26 at 11:00 a.m. She congratulated Krista Oberholtzer
City Council Minutes  6  February 23, 2021
 for being named Employee of the Year, and gave a shout out to Mark Nix to thank him for the
information he gives her for her newsletter on various drives and activities that are going on in the
City. Lastly, she thanked law enforcement members for the public safety efforts regarding crime
within the City and she encouraged residents to park their cars in their garage to prevent theft.

Mayor Kelley

Mayor Kelley announced that on Saturday March 6 there will be another drive through grocery
distribution hosted by Saddleback Church and the City to provide free food for those in need from
9:00 a.m. to 11:00 a.m. at Los Alisos Intermediate School. She stated that at the last food
distribution they were able to provide food to 346 families. Mayor Kelley wanted to make sure
residents are aware that the Saddleback Valley Unified School District is considering a board action
on March 11 to merge the students from Cordillera Elementary School into Montevideo Elementary
School. There will be another use for the Cordillera campus. Announced that the new Annual
Report for 2020 is now available. She thanked both former Director of Community Relations/City
Clerk Karen Hamman and Graphic Artist Toni Nunez for a great job.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:09 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting in Memory of Russ Eastman to Tuesday, March 9, 2021, at
5:00 p.m.
